name: ma1_gapped_bar_lpc_exclusion
description: AC-1 (MA-1) golden -- Scenario B from r1-review's empirical correction (ADDENDUM 7 @ cd7e668d): a genuine gapped intraday bar (a ticker with NO bar entry for a given tick -- e.g. a trading halt or data gap, distinct from a missing prior-session close) must stamp last_percent_change=None for that ticker/tick (excluded from run_monte_carlo's current_symphony_return sum) while a SIBLING ticker that DOES have a bar the same tick still gets its real, finite last_percent_change stamped (included). This is a DIFFERENT code branch from the missing-prior-close case (tests/math_engine/test_ma1_replay_per_tick_lpc_stamping.py's test_missing_prior_close_does_not_raise_or_produce_non_finite_lpc, which exercises yesterday_closes.get(ticker, c) falling back to c -> ret=0.0, a real included-as-zero value) -- the outer per-ticker guard `if ticker in intraday_by_date[date_str] and i < len(intraday_by_date[date_str][ticker])` is what gates this scenario, not the y_close lookup. Both branches were independently found correct by construction; only this gapped-bar branch was previously untested (the plan's own Edge Cases section names 'missing/gapped bars (holiday, half-day)' explicitly).

ticks.note: both tickers have a bar this tick -- baseline, both get a real (zero, at prior close) lpc
BBB has NO bar entry this tick -- a genuine gap (trading halt / data gap). AAA still has one and must get its real per-tick lpc; BBB must be excluded (None), never a fabricated 0.0 or a crash.

derivation: Verified live against the real synthetic_history.build_replay_day (not assumed): at tick 1, AAA's stamped last_percent_change = (101.0 - 100.0) / 100.0 = 0.01 exactly (same formula as the non-gapped golden), while BBB -- which has no bar entry for tick 1 in intraday_by_date -- gets last_percent_change=None (dict.get default; tick_lpc never receives a BBB entry because the outer `if ticker in intraday_by_date[date_str] and i < len(...)` guard is False for that ticker/tick). No exception raised, no NaN/inf produced. This reproduces r1-review's independent empirical finding exactly (ADDENDUM 7).
